request: Revise Memories, game, Plushie, monster and Affection copy; show sent gifts and Surprises in Moments

implemented.memories: [actor] answered a question in memories room
implemented.games: You and [partner] played [real game title]; lightweight lookup matches all 70 current game titles
implemented.plushie: You squished [partner]'s plushie N times / [partner] squished your plushie N times; one uses 1 time
implemented.monsters: [actor] tamed "[monster name]"; names match the current eight-monster Release Room catalogue
implemented.affection: gratitude: thank you; miss_you: “miss you”; spicy: [actor] sent [recipient] some heat 🔥
implemented.gift: [actor] sent [recipient] a gift 🎁 · [Product Type]-[Product Name], including Wallpaper-Green Sage. New records snapshot public product category/title; older events resolve catalogue names when available. Missing historical metadata never exposes internal IDs or invents product names.
implemented.surprise: [actor] sent [recipient] a surprise. A first sent_at transition inserts one event in the existing paid-completion transaction; prepare/upload/open/receipt retries do not create another event.
implemented.notificationReadiness: Both event types enter the existing server attention metadata, client classification, scoped Moments cache hydration and notification-readiness pipeline. The existing moment_events broadcast wakes both users without adding another notification system.
implemented.historicalSurprises: No mass backfill or retroactive notifications: the new trigger records successful sends after migration 251 is installed.
implemented.unchanged: Prices, quotas, delivery, claim behavior, purchase receipts, relation authorization, Adventure journal content and fixed Tap Your Day ordering

databaseCoverage: First committed Surprise send creates exactly one pair/version-scoped Moment
Prepare, incomplete media, repeat completion, open and receipt recovery do not duplicate Moments or spending
Moment insertion failure rolls back Surprise sent state and spending together
Gift label snapshot survives rename and duplicate insert retries
Migration repeatability, trigger-function privilege restrictions, existing gift claim/replace atomicity and Surprise history isolation
